title: Anuj Shrivatri Becomes India's 100th Grandmaster as Modi Hails a Chess Century
excerpt: The 22-year-old from Madhya Pradesh won the 7th ASEAN+ Open in the Philippines with 7 points from 9 rounds to claim the title, 38 years after Viswanathan Anand became India's first Grandmaster. Prime Minister Modi called it a century for Indian chess.
body:
• Anuj Shrivatri, 22, of Madhya Pradesh became India's 100th chess Grandmaster by winning the 7th ASEAN+ Open Chess Championship in Ozamiz City, Philippines, on Sunday.
  • He scored 7 points from 9 rounds, recovering from an opening-round defeat to finish alone in first, half a point ahead of Vietnam's Nguyen Duc Hoa.
  • Shrivatri is the first Grandmaster from Madhya Pradesh; India's first was Viswanathan Anand in 1988.
  • Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated him on X, calling India's hundred Grandmasters a reflection of the talent and hard work of its players.

Indian chess reached a milestone on Sunday as Anuj Shrivatri became the country's 100th Grandmaster by winning the 7th ASEAN+ Open Chess Championship in the Philippines, Chess.com reported. The 22-year-old recovered from an opening-round defeat to finish alone in first place with 7 points from 9 rounds, scoring seven points from his final eight games.

How the Title Was Won

Shrivatri's final-round win against IM James Morris of Australia clinched both the tournament and the Grandmaster title, Chess.com reported. He finished half a point ahead of Vietnam's Nguyen Duc Hoa, according to the PTI report carried by NewKerala. Shrivatri, who held the International Master title, is the first Grandmaster from Madhya Pradesh.

"India has hit a century in chess! Exceptional isn't it? India is now home to a hundred chess Grandmasters! Congratulations to Anuj Shrivatri on becoming India's 100th Chess Grandmaster! What a wonderful achievement it is."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister, on X

Modi said the milestone reflected the immense talent, dedication and hard work of India's players and the growing popularity of chess among the country's youth, and that it was heartening to see young talent emerging from different parts of the country.

Thirty-Eight Years From One to a Hundred

Shrivatri's title comes 38 years after Viswanathan Anand earned his to become India's first Grandmaster in 1988, before going on to win five world championship titles. Chess.com noted that FIDE's November list includes 97 Indian Grandmasters, with Shrivatri, Ethan Vaz and Rathanvel V S awaiting formal confirmation of their titles, which is how the count reaches a hundred. India ranks fourth among federations by total Grandmasters, behind Russia, the United States and Germany, on the November FIDE figures Chess.com cited.

What It Shows

The geography of the milestone is part of the story: the hundredth title went not to Chennai or another established chess centre but to a player from Madhya Pradesh claiming his state's first. For diaspora families whose children play FIDE-rated chess in the US, Britain and the Gulf, the Indian system that produced a hundred Grandmasters in under four decades remains the benchmark, and its newest member arrived by winning a tournament outright, the hardest way to earn the title.
